problem: Given the transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+y+z \\ z+y-x \\ z-2y\end{aligned}],$ find its rank.

activity_context.topic_title: The Image and Rank of a Linear Transformation

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Rank of a Linear Transformation
examples.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071327/assets/71adf512017629aa4cfc010c18bc840ea63459818bae4ebc0b7dba59193c0d00.png) is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ then what is $\text{rank}(\mathbf{T})?$
examples.worked_solution:
In general, $\text{rank}(\mathbf{T}) = \text{dim}(\text{Im}(\mathbf{T})) = \text{rank}(T).$ 

So, we need to find the rank of the matrix $T.$ We reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ -6 & 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 7 & 7 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{7}{4}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $T$ has $2$ pivot columns, we have that 

$$
\textrm{rank}(\mathbf{T})=\textrm{rank}(T)=2.
$$

feedback.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{4}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{4}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}-{x}_{3},$ where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{4} \\ 2{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{3}+4{x}_{4} \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}-3{x}_{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b]$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 6 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -1 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get the false statement $0=-6.$ Therefore, the system is inconsistent, and we conclude that  $b\notin \text{Im}(T).$
